— FNATIC (@FNATIC) November 17, 2026.

For the UK scene, the scale of change matters. Fnatic is one of the LEC’s best-supported clubs among British fans.

Sources indicate that the club has also opened a search for a League of Legends General Manager. Its job advert claims Fnatic goes into a rebuild in 2027. The new hire will run recruitment of players, coaches and staff, including transfers and benchings, and will manage the team’s budget.

Habby is a developer and publisher that has released some neat little mobile games over the years. You may recall Archero One and Two, as well as Dicero and Capybara Go! Now, Habby are once more tackling the roguelike genre, and fusing it with tower defence as pre-registration opens for Monster Must Die!

Monster Must Die, as mentioned above, mashes up two genres with tower defence and roguelike. You start each battle with a summoning tower, then gradually introduce up to four heroes to fight off near-endless waves of monsters.

The world could always use more heroes Of course, as you might expect, Monster Must Die takes some cues from Vampire Survivors, especially in having the myriad of strategies and skills that you can combo together to take on the forces of evil! That means plenty of opportunities to tinker with builds.

According to recent reports, and Habby are also eager to point out you have effectively unlimited stamina, meaning that you won't need to worry about waiting on timers to get back into the fight. You'll certainly need that stamina to take on the hordes and power up by visiting the Dungeon.

Recent findings suggest that overall, Monster Must Die looks like a lot of Habby's other releases: a perfectly competent take on a tried-and-true genre. About the only thing I can say is that it doesn't do much to stand out otherwise. Hopefully, when it does release, we'll see it making more of an impression, but for now it's just worth keeping an eye on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!

It has been revealed that show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.

It has been revealed that per the Steam page, it claims to have turned the above advert format into a whole newly introduced "deeply strategic genre", the "gates shooter", by stirring in "elements of roguelikes and bullet heavens". I need somebody to authenticate whether this is a truthful statement, or developer TinyToad pulling a fast one. In the meantime, I'll say that 1) I have now managed to kill several ogres, 2) I like Korridor's electro-metal soundtrack.

Sources indicate that in Korridor, you're a bald medieval monk garbed in Poundshop Adeptus Astartes platemail. You've woken up in a dungeon of mysterious provenance, and must walk very slowly down its corridors korridors while shooting and punching goblins, wraiths and demons hurrying the other way. Each enemy has a numerical health indicator, and the basic challenge is working out whether you can empty it before they walk into you – which costs you a proportionate amount of health, mitigated by armour. As you go, you'll walk through a choice of gates that grant buffs such as faster health regen, bullet penetration, or nippier horizontal motion.

The fact that you don't control how fast the monk trudges vertically allows the game to synch the onslaught pretty tightly to the thudding, growling score. It reminds me a little of Thumper, though it isn't nearly so invigoratingly malevolent. So far. At intervals, the beat thickens and all the enemies burst into a sprint, throwing their arms up and conveying the strong impression that they are more running away from something than running at you. There's clearly a dreadful entity at the far end of the dungeon. Perhaps it is another overdressed monk with an even bigger gun.

In a recent development, is this how those mobile games actually work? If it is, then alas and alack, all is lost. I've finally succumbed to those adverts, and all it took was some disingenuous Steam copy promising to place them at a critical remove. Curse you, TinyToad. Curse you and your gates. If you were actually a toad, I'd step on you. Still, now that we've broken the ice, can you please make another game in which I get to play one of those gloating giantesses in Hero Wars? Because I know some people who dig that kind of thing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nintendo has issued a statement acknowledging load time complications on Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy on Switch 2.

The organization has promised to released a patch addressing the concerns, citing the long load times that primarily occur when travelling to surface areas. It's also identified an issue in which long loads occur if your network connection is unstable.

While Nintendo works to resolve the issues, it has advised to play in an environment with a stable network connection.

"In Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy, we have identified an concern where loading times are longer than expected when traveling to surface areas, including the Rescue Camp. We are at the moment preparing an patch to address this. We apologise for any inconvenience this may cause.

Recent findings suggest that "Additionally, we have identified an concern where launching the game or accessing the "Dandori Challenge" (Dandori Test) may take an extended amount of time if the network connection is unstable. We are presently investigating the cause of this issue.

"If you encounter these complications, playing in an environment with a stable network connection may help resolve them.".

Industry observers note that pikmin 4 on Switch 2 garnered decent reviews upon release, though it's safe to say that it's not the most beloved revision Nintendo has provided for its latest console. Players were immediately put off by the load times, a lack of 60fps, and seemingly slight upcoming content based on existing levels.

Indeed, Nintendo's latest statement has been met with comments from users demanding that 60fps be added to the game, but the firm has not acknowledged this, so it seems unlikely to be included at this time.

It has been revealed that are you happy to see Nintendo acknowledge these concerns? Will a patch improve your own enjoyment? Let us know with a comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Sources indicate that unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically rolled out first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Sources indicate that another substantial reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

In a recent development, the demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nongshim RedForce have brought 2022 world champion Deft back to the LCK and paired him again with Kingen and Pyosik. The move follows an eighth-place 2026 for the club and comes days after BLG ended Korea's four-year hold on the World Championship.

Industry observers note that kim ‘Deft’ Hyuk-kyu’s signing was confirmed on 19 November. The club used its official social media channels to make the announcement. Deft began his military service after the 2024 season ended.

The deal reunites him with two members of the DRX side that won the 2022 World Championship. Jungler Hong ‘Pyosik’ Chang-hyeon joined later the same day, alongside support Moon ‘Andil’ Gwan-bin. Top laner Hwang ‘Kingen’ Seong-hoon had re-signed a day earlier.

Deft’s signing was announced at 7pm. The Pyosik and Andil additions that followed completed Nongshim’s five-man starting line-up, Inven Global reported. Mid laner Seon ‘Calix’ Hyeon-bin provides continuity. He has been with the organisation since 2021 and extended his deal on 18 November.

Deft brings a long winning record. He made his debut with MVP Blue in 2013. His titles include the LCK, the LPL, the Mid-Season Invitational and the 2022 World Championship.

According to recent reports, kingen first joined Nongshim for the 2025 season. Pyosik arrives after a difficult 2026 at DN SOOPers. That team lost a run of matches, and rookie Sharvel took his starting place.

Sources indicate that the move had been signalled. About a month before the announcement, Sheep Esports reported from Korean sources that Nongshim planned to sign Deft. The same report said rookie AD carry Diable would need a fresh team.

The signings mark a sharp change of direction after a poor year. Once the league campaign was over, the team lasted just a single match in the play-ins.

According to recent reports, the deal lands days after a setback for the whole league. Bilibili Gaming’s victory over Gen.G came at the Barclays Center in New York. It gave the organisation its first Summoner’s Cup.

Industry observers note that BLG won all four of its series against LCK teams at the tournament. Every LCK seed fell to the Chinese side on its way to the trophy. The title is also the LPL’s first since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

'Deft' has signed a contract as the new ADC of NS RedForce LCK Team.

Please look forward to and support Deft, who has written latest history with an unbreakable spirit through countless trials, as he takes on new challenges and delivers great… pic.twitter.com/bHa1uJWwKV.

— NS RedForce (@NS_RedForce) November 19, 2026.

For Nongshim, a line-up built around three 2022 champions now has an international calendar to aim at. Riot Games has moved First Stand 2027 from Southeast Asia to China and renamed it First Stand: All In. It will be a one-off expanded edition with more teams and players.

Spain gets its debut as a Mid-Season Invitational host in 2027, with Valencia’s Feria de Valencia as the venue. Before that, Riot looks to publish First Stand: All In’s format and qualification process in January.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, GTA 6 is and will continue to have a huge cultural impact for years to come. What I wasn’t expecting was for the game to seemingly affect house prices. That appears to be what has happened to a home listed for sale in Key Largo, Florida, simply because it kind of looks like the house you start your journey in with Jason.

Complex appears to be the cause of the listing going viral. The account shared side-by-side images of the real house in Key Largo and Jason’s in GTA 6, boldly confirming that the former was the inspiration for the latter.

Realtormoc, a real estate account on Instagram, has also shared information about the property, which is listed on Zillow, with GTA 6 fans having a little fun with it in the replies. Most of them are jokes about Brian, the character who owns the house in the game, trying to make some extra cash from it, while my personal favorite reply is the one that reads, “Hey, I forgot something under the floorboards, I’ll call by at the weekend .”.

It has been revealed that the house is listed for $739,000, which appears to be quite a bit more than it was worth as recently as a month or two ago. Zillow’s “Zestimate” for the two-bedroom home is $675,000, so the asking price is considerably higher. Those who have played through the first chapter of GTA 6 know damn well that Jason and Lucia weren’t living in a house worth that much, and that’s because despite the viral hype surrounding this real-life house that kind of resembles the one from GTA 6, it isn’t the house that inspired Jason’s starter home at all.

Sources indicate that that house has already been discovered by people far more talented than those who saw a blue house in Florida on stilts and connected two very distant dots. Shared by GTABOOM, the house that almost certainly inspired Jason’s much more weathered waterfront home is hundreds of miles away from this one. That’s according to GTA mapping sites that used GTADB to reach that conclusion.

The house that’s more likely to be the one Rockstar used to create Jason’s is far smaller and less looked after, as opposed to the shiny, polished house on stilts you can buy for an inflated $739,000. The potentially real Jason house isn’t for sale, but is estimated to be worth around $257,000, which seems far more fitting for the type of life Jason and Lucia have at the start of the game.

It has been revealed that if you were to walk around Key Largo, you would almost certainly see dozens of houses that look like they’ve been ripped right out of GTA 6 because Key Lento, the fictional starting point of the game, is based on that particular part of Florida. It’s only because the $739k house is blue and listed for sale that it has been arbitrarily and falsely dubbed the house that inspired Jason’s in GTA 6.

#167975. World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1838 w)

World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1838 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I don't play video games regularly anymore.
  • Industry observers note that here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019.
  • My relationship with Azeroth began in 2007, when I was ten years old.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth, the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a fresh legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Industry observers note that here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a fresh Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.

My relationship with Azeroth began in 2007, when I was ten years old. As soon as I inserted the CD-ROM, I knew that I was going to have to vastly increase my timeshare on the family desktop. For the next six years, school attendance, sleep, and quality family time suffered immensely as I battled to balance my upcoming parallel existence as a member of the Orcish Horde.

Industry observers note that it's unremarkable now, but the fact that characters created at WoW's launch are now 22 years old and can still be played in the latest iteration of the game would have been almost inconceivable to many developers at the turn of the century. In the late 1990s and early 2000s, the video game industry was overwhelmingly organised around discrete releases expected to have relatively short lives. For most games, commercial success was concentrated in a brief period surrounding their launch, after which sales declined and eventually ceased. WoW's extraordinary success, and exceedingly long half-life, demonstrated the commercial possibilities and durability of a different model: an evolving, immersive digital environment that players paid to inhabit, year after year. Rather than simply purchasing a finished product, players entered a world that would continue to grow around them. Fresh players, after buying the game (and then its subsequent expansions) and paying for a subscription, could begin their adventures in the same world as those who had been there from the beginning, making their way through its ever-expanding geography and history.

According to recent reports, the persistence of Azeroth has been the main driver of its abiding allure for me. I have returned to the game time after time, often just to be enveloped in an audiovisual environment that I know so intimately, and which was so formative in my life. But as the WoW universe was continually developed, the game became increasingly unrecognisable from the version I skipped school to play on Windows XP.

Recent findings suggest that what I wanted from the game had also changed. In a turn that would have been completely anathema to my teenage self, I no longer cared about reaching the endgame or having the most competitive character. I stopped caring about the latest raiding content or PvP rankings. Instead, the elements of the game I had once feverishly tried to skip over, like levelling, professions and story, became, ironically, the only parts of the game that I yearned for.

Sources indicate that as time unspooled, WoW naturally needed updates to stay fresh. This meant overhauling many of the unwieldy elements of its original design. Much of this was described as 'streamlining' the player experience, making the game less tedious by reducing downtime and, most critically, reliance on other players.

The original Azeroth emulated the real world in ways that few contemporary games do. Firstly, it was openly unbalanced, with some classes vastly stronger than others, some of which were borderline unplayable. Secondly, it required extraordinary amounts of patience and downtime to navigate. Most importantly, though, it required collaboration with others to get the most out of it. In order to access the latest content, players would have to self-organise into specifically composed groups as big as 40 players large, and schedule lengthy chunks of time each week to make progress.

Over time, much of the original social architecture that forced player collaboration was stripped from the game. Adventurers no longer needed to search for and group up with other players from their own server to complete rewarding content. Automated matchmaking systems increasingly did the work for them.

I remember many late nights when I was prevented from doing something quite modest because there were simply not enough players online, or not enough of the right classes. With my ambitions frustrated, I would often have no choice but to log off and try again in the morning. These frustrations were, I only learnt in retrospect, an important byproduct of inhabiting a world that did not exist solely for my benefit. Other people had their own schedules, priorities and ambitions, and my experience of the game depended on those contingencies.

The changes to WoW followed the trajectory of the wider online gaming industry, where players could increasingly be matched instantly with others at any time of day. These were changes that genuinely respected players' time, but the texture and immersion of the game world paid a hefty price. In making the game more convenient, Blizzard had also made it less necessary, and in some respects less possible, to participate in the social world that had once made Azeroth feel so alive.

It became increasingly clear that there was a subset of players, like me, who weren't interested in seeing an old dog learn fresh tricks, and just wanted to spend time with the old girl we'd raised from a pup. Even if she did walk slowly, and was a bit blind.

It has been revealed that as the years went on, many players moved on with their lives, even if they continued to carry some indelible residue of Azeroth with them. Others created unofficial instances of the original game, known as private servers, and relived those infant years with a knowledge of the world that they could scarcely have imagined possessing when they first entered it. As these servers became increasingly popular, Blizzard, originally very reluctant, eventually introduced Classic in 2019, an official revival of the game in something approaching its original 2004 form. Since then, legacy versions of WoW have become popular enough to exist alongside the modern game as a major branch of the franchise.

Re-releasing these legacy versions has been a considerable commercial success. But it also exposed a problem with the project of preservation. The original game, because it is so timeworn, has effectively been 'solved.' Players know almost everything about it, including its most obscure idiosyncrasies, and have found ingenious ways of exploiting them. The uncertainty that once made Azeroth feel so vast and mysterious has been replaced by an extraordinary collective expertise. When new content was added to the game, even the best guilds would spend weeks making no progress. During those early years, players at Azeroth's frontiers had to innovate to find creative ways of tackling novel and seemingly intractable problems.

There are clear limits to simulating a turning back of the clock. Players like me slowly realised that we didn't simply want to return to an earlier, simpler period in Azeroth. We wanted something impossible. Like the characters in Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, we wanted to forget what we already knew so that we might experience our birth in Azeroth for the first time all over again.

WoW: Forever is an attempt to solve this problem. Like Old School RuneScape, Forever's undeniable forerunner and a considerable success in its own right, it is an expanded re-release of the original game that imagines an alternate future for Azeroth: one in which the game continues to evolve without abandoning the original texture and mechanics, and one that preserves the social architecture that made it so enriching in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that as I write this, my Orc Warrior is sitting at a Campfire, a newly introduced mechanic that allows players to establish communal campsites and contribute profession-specific items that confer temporary bonuses to themselves and others. To receive a benefit from Campfires, adventurers are forced to sit together, a deliberate attempt from Blizzard to encourage interactions between players. It is too early to tell how effective this socialising mechanism will be in the long run, but nearly everyone in my experience so far has been eager to shoot the breeze together. I have already shared a number of conversations with other players, most of whom are thirty- or forty-somethings on a similar nostalgia quest as me.

According to recent reports, I am playing the game on a laptop using a trackpad, caring very little about efficient or optimal progression. Although I suspect a substantial proportion of the player base shares my approach, not everyone has approached the game so casually. At least five players have already reached maximum level, and many others will have meticulously theory-crafted plans designed to skip straight to the endgame. This is a good thing, and the game should be able to support players with different goals. It's vital that the game rewards time and effort, but I hope that the modest amount of time I am able to commit will allow me to feel like I am on my own meaningful adventure, and not a weak player who is trailing behind.

Industry observers note that many in the community have come to believe, perhaps wishfully, that Forever might escape the trap of vertical progression, in which each fresh wave of content supersedes and renders older content redundant. Instead, the promise of horizontal progression, where new content expands the range of meaningful activities and rewards available without continually raising the ceiling of character power, has been latched on to by members of the community, even though Blizzard's messaging in this regard has not been totally clear.

For players like me, the appeal of horizontal progression is that Azeroth might once again become a place to inhabit, rather than a race to finish. I want to be able to wander off, pursue some obscure profession, or spend an evening doing very little of consequence without feeling that the rest of the world has left me behind. I know I don't have the time to commit to the endgame hamster wheel, and whether Forever will produce a gameworld that meaningfully accommodates players with such different ambitions remains to be seen. But for now, at least, it feels good to be home.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pocket monsters, just not those ones.

Industry observers note that pre-registration only opened at the end of October, so Bandai hasn't kept anyone waiting long. Digimon Alysion is out now on iOS and Android, finally putting the Digimon Card Game on your phone.

Sources indicate that expect an original story with a brand fresh cast of characters, plus a few Digimon you won't have come across before. It's built to teach you the rules as you play through it. The tutorial covers how cards are laid out and used, along with the basics of a battle.

It has been revealed that your collection mixes cards from the physical Digimon Card Game with new ones made for Alysion. On top of that, you’ve got Shiny Cards, Alt-Art Cards and Premium Alt-Art Cards (the animated ones), and you'll get one free pack a day to build your decks from.

According to recent reports, once you’ve fleshed out your kit, you can take it into ranked against people from around the world, or keep things relaxed and spar against friends and characters from the story instead. Breeding is back as well, for that matter. You can raise Digimon and Digivolve them all the way up to Mega, and there's a Digidex of more than 100 entries to fill in.

Pokémon TCG Pocket is the obvious comparison, and probably the reason Digimon Alysion is arriving now at all. The difference is that Bandai isn't starting from scratch, and if you've been playing the physical version, you'll recognise a fair bit of what’s part of your packs.

Bandai has already done something similar with Dragon Ball's Fusion World, which you can play digitally and on paper, so it's a fairly safe bet the game is meant to send some people towards the physical cards too.

Digimon Alysion is free-to-play with in-app purchases on the App Store and Google Play, and a launch event, Battle Carnival Dukemon Ver., is running now.

If you're after more cards to collect, check out our list of the best card games on iOS.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty to do, from battling the Prince of Darkness to rescuing members of Congress caught in sex swing accidents. Between all the zany and off-the-wall shenanigans, sometimes the most fun encounters happen right in your own backyard.

In a recent development, hidden within the humble little town of Hamlet is a wrestling legend ready to take on all challengers, while putting his own pride on the line. If you’re up to snuff and want to become the next Backyard Wrestling Champion, read on to claim your spoils.

In a recent development, in order to find the Champ, you’ll need to head back to Hamlet once you regain control of Jason in Chapter 2. Head to the street between the grocery store and the gas station towards the middle of town. Look for the backyard of one of the houses containing a ring, a trailer, and a major Backyard Wrestling banner.

It has been revealed that knock on the door of the trailer to get some dialogue from the Champ, where he’ll refuse to come out. Toss a nearby can or bottle, then knock again for him to make his entrance, toss Jason to the ground, and drag him into the ring for a little one-on-one playtime. If you can last against the Gentrifier, you’ll be the fresh Champ.

In a recent development, once he’s introduced himself, the Gentrifier will put Jason into a series of grapple-based Quick Time Events. Make sure you boost your Stamina with a drink or snack of some kind before you get started to ensure you’ve got as much time to mash as possible.

Sources indicate that once you clear two of these mash-fests, the Gentrifier will toss Jason to the ground before going for his finishing move, the Eviction Notice. React with Square on PS5/X on XBOX to dive out of the wave, leaving him open for a counter. Don’t waste your time stomping on him. Instead, climb the same post he tried to use, and end it with a soaring People’s Elbow.

Recent findings suggest that once he’s down and out, you can ransack his trailer for some cash, some drugs, his own stylin’ shades, and a one-of-one Luchador mask that can serve as a disguise for either character. A fantastic little token of a victory hard-fought, cementing Jason as the Backyard Wrestling Champion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports. The non-partner organisation is now one win from the playoffs that decide a guaranteed São Paulo Kickoff place.

The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10 UTC on Saturday 21 November, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

Industry observers note that the result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that said it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

The Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

According to recent reports, shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

Across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

Industry observers note that the organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

According to recent reports, the prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

The MOBA genre is competitive in every sense and Quantic Dream is trying to break into it with a Magic the Gathering-esque spin on the format. Players build a deck of cards before queuing into teams of 3, then face off as battling mages, summoning creatures, building fortifications and casting spells rather than choosing a Hero with unique abilities in the traditional MOBA style.

Beta content includes a fresh map, 6 new spells and 5 new summon creatures for your deck, as well as 3 new buildings too.

Industry observers note that also upcoming for this second closed beta is an introduction and tutorial for some of the game’s finer details, as well as a text chat for strategising and much-needed player reporting system to go with it. It will also feature early versions of the Spellcaster customisation system and ranked matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No Org No Problem won the opening and deciding maps against Stallions Esports to reach the MENA Qualifier Playoffs grand final. One more series win against Mix My Miks would send them to VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027 in Berlin alongside partner teams including Fnatic.

According to recent reports, against Stallions Esports, the semi-final went the full distance. No Org No Problem took the opening map in 48 minutes. Stallions Esports levelled on the second, winning a 54-minute contest. No Org No Problem then closed out the decider in 43 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that the result came against a ranked opponent. Stallions Esports sat at rank 72 in the Elo power rankings, with a rating of 1628 and a 24-14 record in 38 rated matches. No Org No Problem are unranked. Stallions had also arrived in mixed form, with two 0-2 defeats to VillianArc in VCL MENA: Resilience Pulse Stage Middle East 2026. They beat Spire Esports twice and AXE in the same competition.

It has been revealed that no Org No Problem reached the playoffs by winning Middle East Qualifier 1, held from 9 to 11 November, with The Spiders finishing second. Stallions Esports won Middle East Qualifier 2 from 16 to 18 November, ahead of Mayhem. Mix My Miks won North Africa Qualifier 1, a single-elimination event from 9 to 11 November, ahead of BAAM Esports. Each of those qualifiers had 64 teams.

Mix My Miks booked their final place by beating Gamax Esports in the second semi-final. That match also went to three maps. The four-team playoffs are being played online in a single-elimination bracket. The semi-finals were best of three.

Alongside the MENA winner, Europe sends two qualifiers to Berlin and Türkiye sends one. The partner teams already in the field are BBL Esports, Fnatic, FUT Esports, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp, Team Heretics, Team Liquid and Team Vitality. Fnatic were confirmed in October 2026 as staying on as a VCT EMEA partner for 2027.

In a recent development, the tournament will be played in person at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin in early 2027. For the MENA winner, the trip carries direct financial value. Riot’s support for non-partner teams starts at Kickoff, and the sums rise for teams that progress further through the season.

Non-partner teams that qualify for Masters receive US$200,000, and those reaching Champions receive US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. Europe’s route to Kickoff runs in parallel. The Europe Kickoff Qualifier Playoffs begin with a Swiss stage from 25 to 29 November, followed by playoffs from 3 to 5 December.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the employment tribunal over Rockstar's firing of 34 workers last year has come to an end for now, pending a final verdict from the judge.
  • In a recent development, that's according to People Make Games' Chris Bratt, who's reported on the tribunal throughout the proceedings."I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case," he cited judge Lucy Wiseman as having stated following closing arguments from Rockstar and the union representing the fired staff over the past couple of days.
  • Bratt reported that could mean anything from weeks to a few months of waiting, leaving the fired staff looking at more time in the limbo they've occupied throughout the tribunal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the employment tribunal over Rockstar's firing of 34 workers last year has come to an end for now, pending a final verdict from the judge. Said judge hasn't offered a concrete estimate of when her judgement will arrive, but has reportedly asserted that she'll provide it "as swiftly as [she] possibly can".

In a recent development, that's according to People Make Games' Chris Bratt, who's reported on the tribunal throughout the proceedings."I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case," he cited judge Lucy Wiseman as having stated following closing arguments from Rockstar and the union representing the fired staff over the past couple of days. "What I will say is that I will use my best [endeavours] to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can.".

Bratt reported that could mean anything from weeks to a few months of waiting, leaving the fired staff looking at more time in the limbo they've occupied throughout the tribunal.

To recap the arguments Wiseman will have heard, Rockstar accused the fired staff of leaking "confidential information on a public forum", while the Independent Workers’ union of Great Britain (IWGB) union have accused Rockstar of being motivated by union busting in letting the workers go. According to a previous report from People Make Games, discussion of a new company Slack policy in a union-run Discord server preceded the firings.

The fired devs haven't called for supporters to boycott GTA 6 - the game they were working on prior to being let go - in solidarity, but instead to consider buying specially-designed union t-shirts, the proceeds of which will go towards the workers' "Fighting Fund".

Devs still at Rockstar and the IWGB have formed the Rockstar Games Workers Union since their fired colleagues' tribunal proceedings began and are in the midst of a vote on union recognition as of writing.

It has been revealed that writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section this week, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte expressed that it's "hard not to worry about what the future holds" for developers at the studio, with the prospect of layoffs potentially happening now the significant game is out the door concerning staff. Uriarte made clear that, as of the writing of his piece, Rockstar staff "have had no indication that layoffs are coming".

As we head towards the weekend, it's becoming increasingly cold and dark, and that means you'll probably want to sit and find a mobile game to sink plenty of time into. Well, you're in luck, because there's a constant glut of great latest releases, including the launch of Dicevaders on iOS!

It has been revealed that dicevaders sees you taking on the role not of defender of the Earth, but of its invaders and destroyers. To do so, you'll need to gradually overwhelm the defences of each of Earth's bastions, and you'll do so with dice (naturally). In essence, you place units, build up multipliers and gradually overcome the defence rating of each planet to destroy it.

It makes for a rather interesting combination of luck and strategy, where you'll need to think about when you might need to reroll and keep your supply of currencies stocked up to do so. The graphics are, of course, the kind of crunchy, colourful pixels I'm fond of, so you won't hear any complaints from me, and the mix of blues, purples and reds makes for a thoroughly alien colour palette.

There's plenty of synergy, different commanders and units to take advantage of too. So if you're looking for a game with plenty of depth to enjoy this winter, why not check out Dicevaders on iOS?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright.
  • If you couldn’t guess already, the fresh theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.
  • The major new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the fresh theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The major new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

The Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

According to recent reports, the other major addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

It has been revealed that chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

Recent findings suggest that as with every major enhancement, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

QoR's 2-0 win over Maryville University completed a recovery from an opening defeat at the VCT Americas Kickoff North America qualifiers. A Kickoff place and a Red Bull Home Ground spot both stay within QoR's reach as a result.

The line-up of ExpMoe, calamity, vanitas, yearn and dynamic was one of eight teams Riot Games invited directly to the North America Qualifier Playoffs. Cloud9, ENVY and two Shopify Rebellion line-ups were also on that list.

Before facing Maryville, QoR edged Shopify Rebellion Gold 2-1 in round two. In the Swiss stage, two wins sent a team through and two losses knocked it out. QoR sit 99th in the Elo power rankings, with a rating of 1590 and a 37-34 record across 71 rated matches.

Maryville came through the second open qualifier, held from 12 to 15 November, which drew 512 teams. They finished in the top two of that bracket. They then opened this event by sweeping Shopify Rebellion Gold.

A 0-2 loss to Cloud9 followed, and defeat by QoR left them with two losses. In the other round-three matches, Oafs beat SaD Esports, counterfeit beat FlyQuest and Wildcard beat Winthrop, each without dropping a map. The Elo table places Maryville 161st, with a rating of 1521 and a 6-7 record in 13 rated matches.

Recent findings suggest that the playoffs are an eight-team double-elimination bracket. The winner takes North America’s direct place at the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in São Paulo. The runner-up goes to the Americas Last Chance Qualifier, also in São Paulo, on 17 and 18 December. That event is the last route into Kickoff. Eight partner teams are invited to Kickoff, and four places go to non-partner teams.

Sources indicate that riot runs the North America qualifiers with Red Bull. They also serve as the North America qualifiers for Red Bull Home Ground. The Los Angeles event runs from 10 to 13 December. Ten teams will play for a total prize pool of $100,000 USD. Eight are invited from around the world, and two earn their places through regional qualifiers. Riot will also reveal the 2027 Kickoff draws live on stage there.

In a recent development, fnatic are EMEA’s invited team. The organisation is rebuilding its roster after parting with several players, including long-serving captain Jake ‘Boaster’ Howlett, Red Bull noted.

Team Cherry Unveils New Original Titles, Sea of Sorrow Release Date

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Team Cherry has done it once again with its eccentric reveals, as its latest livestream presentation Cherry Time has revealed not only the release date for the upcoming DLC for Hollow Knight: Silksong, but also some brand-upcoming original titles.
  • Previously known mostly for the original Hollow Knight, the studio is now expanding its catalogue to actually include some more indie titles from different genres, but not without giving some love to the original game that first made them famous.
  • Sea of Sorrow, a free expansion adding tons of new areas, bosses, challenges, quality-of-life improvements, and some new lore pieces for Silksong, is described as an “expansion like they never did before” and will be dropping on December 11, free for all players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Team Cherry has done it once again with its eccentric reveals, as its latest livestream presentation Cherry Time has revealed not only the release date for the upcoming DLC for Hollow Knight: Silksong, but also some brand-upcoming original titles.

Previously known mostly for the original Hollow Knight, the studio is now expanding its catalogue to actually include some more indie titles from different genres, but not without giving some love to the original game that first made them famous.

Sea of Sorrow, a free expansion adding tons of new areas, bosses, challenges, quality-of-life improvements, and some new lore pieces for Silksong, is described as an “expansion like they never did before” and will be dropping on December 11, free for all players.

The Cherry Time livestream has revealed the latest trailer for the Silksong expansion, complete with its release date and a small tease for its bosses. Just like with the base game, the release date was revealed exactly two weeks before its launch.

Sources indicate that first revealed earlier this week, the stream was a welcome surprise for the fans, filled with latest footage from the new areas Hornet will visit and small showcases of what we can expect in this new adventure. And if we can take the original Hollow Knight expansions as a baseline, we’re in for a huge treat here.

It has been revealed that we can see newly introduced scenes of Hornet running across the new areas and the new enemies she’ll be facing in these distant waters. A favorite of mine is the new pirate-like boss, which is one of the main focuses in this trailer. We can also see some platforming sessions and at least one new of the dreaded enemy gauntlets in the trailer, so get ready to put those tools to use.

Industry observers note that and speaking of tools, the biggest highlight obviously goes to the final scene, where Hornet actually unveils a new tool being used for the most ancient practice in any good RPG: fishing. Love it or hate it, the game wouldn’t be complete without it, and you know it. And in classic Hollow Knight fashion, expect some obscure secret to be hidden beneath the fishing waters.

For now, I’m hoping for more challenging areas such as the Cogwork Core and fewer areas that are just a torture session in a trench coat, such as Bilewater.

In a recent development, aside from Sea of Sorrow news, Team Cherry also promised more “exciting announcements”, and they did deliver. Previously known as the studio that wouldn’t speak with its public while working on their game (in a very justified way), this now seems to be in the past as the small South Australian studio came forward not only with a release date for the expansion, but also with brand-latest titles developed by the studio.

Sources indicate that these include Blokan: Secret of the Walking City, a newly introduced game by Hollow Knight artist Rohan Fraser. It follows a detective solving cases in a traditional puzzle game style above a fantasy-inspired city, fully drawn by hand. It is inspired by the traditional golden age adventure games, according to Fraser himself.

Radio Rain is another one, a side-scrolling title made by Lukas Stobie, who previously developed Rising Dusk. This new side-scrolling adventure game follows the protagonist as she finds her way across the ruins of a rainy world filled with music, all in an amazing pixel art style.

It has been revealed that the final reveal is The Botanist and The Translator, developed by Makoto Kuji (the voice of Hornet herself). In this 2d adventure game, you’ll play as the botanist-investigator Hatti and her animal translator partner Oliver, who work together to unveil a mystery while exploring a beautifully hand-drawn Sailor Moon-inspired world.

Recent findings suggest that it’s amazing to see Team Cherry actually growing up as a studio, as they can now reliably deliver more titles and not be bound to the same franchise for years. While the Hollow Knight games might still be their magnum opus, knowing that we’ll see more of its DNA implemented across different titles is an even better gift than I could’ve asked for. Especially now that Sea of Sorrow is coming.

Hour-long Total War: Warhammer 40,000 campaign stream highlights off ship battle-less fleet management, makes clear how not ideal getting Space Marine armies killed is

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (502 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that try not to get whole armies of Space Marines pasted against the surfaces of planets thanks to your shoddy tactics, please.
  • The stream showed off "an expansion" of the build that devs Creative Assembly let folks like RPS bossman Julian give a go at Gamescom in the summer, via an Ultramarines campaign in a system called Praevoss.
  • Sources indicate that each star system's a "contained campaign", so you hop from one to the next, with certain aspects of your army or skills you've built up carrying over.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that try not to get whole armies of Space Marines pasted against the surfaces of planets thanks to your shoddy tactics, please. So ask the bosses of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, who're keen not to have their training workloads doubled because you're a crap general and have gotten a tight-knit force of uber-tough grunts killed unnecessarily, hope as they watch you play. This and other things have been emphasised by a fresh stream showing off over an hour of campaigning in the strategy warhammerer.

The stream showed off "an expansion" of the build that devs Creative Assembly let folks like RPS bossman Julian give a go at Gamescom in the summer, via an Ultramarines campaign in a system called Praevoss. Described as a middle-of-the-road option in terms of system size, Praevoss is home to three conquerable planets and a couple of others that aren't suitable for stompy unit hijinks.

Sources indicate that each star system's a "contained campaign", so you hop from one to the next, with certain aspects of your army or skills you've built up carrying over. "First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," the devs explained. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start [point], [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do." Creative assembly have also been able to play around a bit more with difficulty as a result of this setup.

Sources indicate that as the stream properly got going, the devs focused on chatting about unit specialisation, fleet movement, fleet actions, fleet transportation and Space Marine fleet buildings. Your fleet takes the form of big ships which can be parked above a continent on a planet and offer support via reinforcements and bombardment. As far as the Space Marines specifically go, they're designed to be a small force that's tough to kill, rather than a massive one that's able to recover more rapidly and aims to overwhelm with sheer numbers as part of its gameplan.

"Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the devs noted, as if sensing some blunder I might make far in the future. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that." At least it looks like I'll not be losing any ships too, since their presence seems limited to providing support to the ground troops, rather than battling each other high above the planets.

As of right now, Total War: Warhammer 40,000 remains without a release date, but can be wishlisted on Steam if you fancy.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that godLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026.
  • Sources indicate that the playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, godLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 in the upper bracket of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier. Only two South Asian sides will reach the Last Chance Qualifier, where a single place at Kickoff in Bangkok is on offer.

Sources indicate that godLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026. GodLike took both maps of the best-of-three upper bracket quarter-final. Trigger Point Esports now drop into the lower bracket of the double-elimination format.

Sources indicate that the playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST. Series in the bracket are played as best-of-three or best-of-five.

Industry observers note that godLike arrived in form. They reached the playoffs with an unbeaten 4-0 record in the open qualifier, VLR.gg reported. They shared joint first to fourth place in that event, which ran from 17 to 20 November. Trigger Point finished in the group placed fifth to eighth.

Industry observers note that godLike fielded Karam1L, Paradox and RvK from India, alongside sayoo from Indonesia and azyshaha from the Philippines. Sabyasachi ‘Antidote’ Bose is listed as head coach, with Samar as substitute. Trigger Point’s listed players are SangraM, WEELJACK and RaJ.

South Asian teams cannot qualify directly for Kickoff. The top two from the playoffs join the Oceania playoff winner and the Southeast Asia playoff runner-up in a four-team Last Chance Qualifier. Only its winner goes through to Kickoff in Bangkok, according to Dot Esports.

The stakes are high. Twelve teams will play at Kickoff, and the top three will qualify for Masters 1. The route stays narrow later in the season too. South Asia has no direct place at the Cups, with Cup 1 in Manila and Cup 2 in Tokyo. It sends two teams to an eight-team Pacific LCQ, and the winner takes the last Cup place.

The qualifier also has a latest organiser. Riot picked JioBLAST to run the South Asia qualifiers instead of NODWIN Gaming, the previous organiser. Riot has not said why it made the change.

Sources indicate that the UK interest lies with SIGN Esports. They beat Zexar Esports 2-0 in another upper bracket quarter-final. Russel ‘Russ’ Mendes joined SIGN Esports on 16 November 2026. He is the only player from the UK in the eight-team playoff field.

Russ was born in 1998 and is of Indian descent. He won the VALORANT Challengers 2025 South Asia Grand Final with Velocity Gaming on 13 July 2025, when they beat S8UL 3-1.

According to recent reports, godLike Esports and SIGN Esports both remain in the upper bracket, one defeat away from the lower bracket. Trigger Point Esports and Zexar Esports must win from the lower bracket to stay in contention for a top-two finish. The playoffs run until 29 November 2026.

While mobile doesn't have an auteur developer on the level of something like Hideo Kojima, by now you've probably noticed there are plenty of names that crop up which we like to cover, such as Bart Bonte or solo developer Ovidiu Tepes, who has just opened the store page for his newest game, Sticky Snap!

It has been revealed that just like Tepes' previous releases, this is a deceptively simple-looking puzzler, but one that has some truly engaging mechanics to it. You play as a slime with three sticky limbs, and have to alternate between them as you travel across levels, dodging obstacles and seeking out your gold coin as you go.

And that, I reckon, is why we like covering Tepes' stuff. It's a throwback to the days of mobile when a solid, original concept done well could become the fresh darling of the app store. Even if now, for better or worse, we have so much more variety.

According to recent reports, sticky Snap! is set to boast 41 different levels, unlockable skins and even a leaderboard. So if you want, you'll be able to prove your puzzling acumen. Keep an eye out for the release of Sticky Snap! on iOS and Android, projected to land January 6th next year!

It has been revealed that in the meantime, if you simply can't wait and need something to play right now, we've got you covered.   • The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for Fresh Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s massive upcoming patch, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in Newly introduced Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for Fresh Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

It has been revealed that the story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two fresh Agents being introduced in this revision belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

According to recent reports, sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a fresh game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this revision also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

Industry observers note that the substantial event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

As always, there’s no reason not to catch up on the latest set of Zenless Zone Zero codes for some free in-game items.
